glosses: a term of respect for a woman who is older than the speaker, but not too old
etym:
Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *akka- (“elder sister”).
Cognates
Cognate with Kannada ಅಕ್ಕ (akka), Malayalam അക്ക (akka), or അക്കൻ (akkaṉ), Telugu అక్క (akka), Tulu ಅಕ್ಕ (akka), ಅಕ್ಕಾ (akkā), or ಅಕ್ಕೆ (akke).

gloss: respectful term of address for any woman older than oneself; madam.
glosses: respectful term of address for any woman older than oneself; madam.
etym: Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *amma (“mother”). Doublet of அம்மை (ammai) and அம்மன் (ammaṉ).
Plural of நீ (nī). Inherited from Old Tamil 𑀦𑀻𑀭𑁰 (nīr), from Proto-South Dravidian *nīr.

From நல் (nal, “good”), from Proto-South Dravidian *nal (“good”). Compare நன்று (naṉṟu).
Cognate with Kannada ನನ್ನಿ (nanni), Malayalam നന്ദി (nandi) / നന്നി (nanni).
Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *ñām (“we”, inclusive). Cognate with Old Kannada ನಾವ್ (nāv), Kannada ನಾವು (nāvu), Kurux नाम (nām), Malayalam നാം (nāṁ).

gloss: please (used in the sense of requesting a little cooperation)
glosses: please (used in the sense of requesting a little cooperation)
etym:
Compare குஞ்சு (kuñcu, “smallness”).
Cognates
Cognate with Kannada ಕೊಂಚ (koñca), Kolami कॊच्च (kocca), Malayalam കൊഞ്ചം (koñcaṁ), Telugu కొంచెము (koñcemu) and Tulu ಕೊಂಡ್ರ (koṇḍra).
From கோ (kō) + -மான் (-māṉ), compare சீமான் (cīmāṉ), எஜமான் (ejamāṉ) and நீதிமான் (nītimāṉ). Ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *kō, cognate with Malayalam കോമാൻ (kōmāṉ).
Plural of அவன் (avaṉ) or அவள் (avaḷ), from அவர் (avar) + -கள் (-kaḷ).

Plural of அவன் (avaṉ) or அவள் (avaḷ), from அ- (a-, distal marker) + -வர் (-var), see Proto-Dravidian *awar.
Cognate with Kannada ಅವರು (avaru), Malayalam അവർ (avaṟ), Telugu వారు (vāru).

Tamil அங்கு (aṅku)

From அங்கு (aṅku, “there”).
From Sanskrit पक्व (pakva).
Plural of நீ (nī), first attested in Middle Tamil: நீங்கள் (nīṅkaḷ). By surface analysis, நீம் (nīm) + -கள் (-kaḷ, plural marker). Cognate with Kannada [Term?], Malayalam നിങ്ങൾ (niṅṅaḷ).
Learned borrowing from Sanskrit ஸ்வாமிந் (svāmin). Doublet of சாமி (cāmi).
Inherited from Old Tamil 𑀢𑀺𑀭𑀼 (tiru), cognate with Malayalam തിരു (tiru). Possibly from Sanskrit श्री (śrī), and if so, a doublet of ஶ்ரீ (śrī).
